clue.text: Display a king's put on in large building

parts.note: to hang pictures is to display them
R is the abbreviation for king (Latin rex)

explanation.surface: A king's exhibition is mounted in some vast hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' just says the pieces are joined: HANG, then A, then R for king.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangar is a huge shed for housing aircraft, so it is a large building.

clue.text: New hairdo, pet, makes you a goddess!

indicators.note: a new version of the words rearranges their letters, the way a new hairdo restyles hair

explanation.surface: A fresh hairstyle turns your darling into a divinity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' tells you to rearrange the letters of HAIRDO and PET together.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite is the Greek goddess of love and beauty.

clue.text: Picked up vessel holding two light metals, and a soft one

indicators.note: the turned vessel holds the metal symbols inside it
in a down clue, picking something up lifts it so it reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a mug is a drinking vessel
AL is the chemical symbol for aluminium, a light metal
LI is the chemical symbol for lithium, the lightest metal

explanation.surface: A ship collected that holds a pair of lightweight metals plus a malleable one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' looks like a sound signal, but in a down clue it turns the vessel upwards to GUM; 'holding' puts the two symbols inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallium is a soft silvery metal that melts in the hand, so it is a soft metal like the others named.

clue.text: Odd game, first in match

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word match is taken

explanation.surface: A strange sport, as the opening of a fixture shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is an old British colloquial word for strange or peculiar.

clue.text: What may be star's most enjoyable time?

definitions.text: What may be star's most enjoyable time?

parts.words: What may be star's most enjoyable time?
parts.note: read literally, a star is a point of light far up in the sky, a lofty spot; the clue's other reading is the best moment of a performer's day

explanation.definitionFit: A highlight or best moment of an occasion is idiomatically its most memorable part, and a star sits at a lofty point in the sky.

clue.text: Room for storing a special sort of meat

indicators.note: the room holds the letter inside it as if storing it

parts.note: a hall is a room

explanation.surface: A room kept for storing a particular kind of meat, like a butcher's cold store.
explanation.definitionFit: Halal meat is slaughtered and prepared according to Islamic law, a special category of meat.

clue.text: Force greedier man to reform

indicators.note: reforming the words reshapes their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Police must make a grasping individual mend his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reform' asks you to rearrange GREEDIER and MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The gendarmerie is the French armed police, a force in the sense of a police body.

clue.text: Country's security system holding information up

indicators.note: the seal holds the turned word inside it

parts.note: a seal secures an envelope or a door against tampering

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A nation's safety network is keeping intelligence under wraps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the information word to NEG, and 'holding' tucks it inside the seal; 'Country's' reads as Country is.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegal is a country in West Africa.

clue.text: Woman novelist had approval in France and Russia

parts.note: oui is French for yes
da is the Russian word for yes, so approval in Russia

explanation.surface: A female writer received a nod of approval in two countries.
explanation.definitionFit: Ouida was the pen name of Maria Louise Ramé, a Victorian woman novelist.

clue.text: Poem with two lines revised, about greeting a nightingale

indicators.note: the reworked letters go about the greeting, which sits inside them
a revised poem has its letters reworked into another order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line, so two lines give LL
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A poet edits two lines of verse in which they salute a songbird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges the poem and two lines into P...LOMEL, and 'about' wraps that round the greeting. Philomel is the poets' nightingale.
explanation.definitionFit: Philomel is the poetic name for the nightingale, from Philomela of Greek myth.

clue.text: Ambassador and sister fronting trade organisation

indicators.note: the first piece goes in front of the second

parts.note: a sister is a nun
CIO is the Congress of Industrial Organizations, a US trade union body

explanation.surface: A diplomat and a nun lead a union federation.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuncio is a papal ambassador to a foreign government.

clue.text: Singing teacher's notes — can solo fit, if revised?

indicators.note: revising the phrase rewrites it, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vocal coach asks whether a solo could be made to fit if rewritten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges CAN, SOLO and FIT; 'if' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonic sol-fa is the do-re-mi system of naming notes used in teaching singing.

clue.text: Devious about holy ceremony in religious style

indicators.note: the devious word goes about the others, enclosing them

parts.note: sly means devious
pi is British slang for pious or holy
a ritual is a ceremony

explanation.surface: Some shady character performs a sacred rite in a pious manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiritually means in a way concerning the spirit or religion, matching in religious style.

clue.text: Paraphernalia in clothes

explanation.surface: Kit for some activity kept among one's garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear means both equipment in general and, informally, the clothes someone wears.

clue.text: An old country is backing America

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word is reversed

explanation.surface: A former nation is said to support the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support, but it turns the word round to SI.
explanation.definitionFit: Siam was the former name of Thailand until 1939, hence an old country.

clue.text: Inadequate earnings — penny rent collected

indicators.note: the earnings collect the other pieces inside them

parts.note: income is earnings
to let a property is to rent it out

explanation.surface: A tenant complains that low wages barely cover the rent being collected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collected' puts penny and rent inside the earnings; 'rent' here is the verb to let out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something incomplete is lacking parts, which makes it inadequate.

clue.text: Firm with good minor employee

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A business with a decent junior worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A cog, as in a cog in the machine, is idiomatically an unimportant worker in a large organisation.

clue.text: Line up for entertainment

parts.note: suggests a queue for a show, but means a cord stretched high in the air for an acrobat's circus act

explanation.definitionFit: A rope stretched high above a circus ring is literally a raised line on which performers walk to entertain.

clue.text: Drink about two litres, and phone campanologist?

indicators.note: the drink goes about the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: beer is a drink
L is the abbreviation for litre, so two give LL
to ring someone is to phone them

explanation.surface: Someone orders a large beer and calls a person who rings church bells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places the litres and the phone call inside the drink; the question mark flags that a bell ringer need not be a scholar of bells.
explanation.definitionFit: Campanology is the art of bell ringing, so a campanologist is one who rings bells.

clue.text: See female having row, being less humble

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: Look at the woman quarrelling, getting rather too proud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel, but here it is a line of seats, a TIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Loftier means haughtier or prouder, the opposite of more humble.

clue.text: Summon an errand-boy

definitions.meaning: to call someone over a loudspeaker or ...
a boy servant who runs messages, as in a hotel

explanation.surface: Call for a lad who runs messages.
explanation.definitionFit: Page means both to summon someone by calling and a young messenger or attendant.

clue.text: Chemist has litmus paper, strangely limp, discarded

indicators.note: letters arranged strangely are scrambled, with those of the other word discarded

explanation.surface: A lab scientist owns some test paper that has gone oddly floppy and been thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' scrambles LITMUS PAPER, and 'discarded' removes the letters of LIMP, leaving the seven needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was a famous French chemist and microbiologist.

clue.text: Boss dismissing one member of kitchen staff

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a chief is a boss
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A manager sacks one of the cooks.
explanation.definitionFit: A chef is a professional cook, a member of a kitchen's staff.

clue.text: Judge with little time for compassion

parts.note: to hear a case is to judge it
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A magistrate with scarcely a moment to spare for mercy.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart can mean compassion or kindness, as in to have a heart.

clue.text: One absorbing endless poetry, one in place of learning

indicators.note: the first word soaks up the others inside it

parts.note: unity is oneness, the number one

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is removed

parts.note: verse is poetry
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone engrossed in poetry without end, studying at an academy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts the poetry word to VERS, and 'absorbing' takes that plus one inside the oneness word.
explanation.definitionFit: A university is an institution of higher education, a place where learning happens.

clue.text: I'd been usher, then sat back

parts.note: an usher leads people, so to have been usher is to have led

explanation.surface: Having shown guests to their seats, I then relaxed.
explanation.definitionFit: Idled means lazed or did nothing, the sense of sitting back.

clue.text: Coming from centre wanting reform, not Conservative

indicators.note: not tells you to leave out the letter for the party

parts.note: a radical wants political reform

explanation.surface: A politician from the middle wants change, but is no Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: Radial means spreading out from a central point, as spokes do.

clue.text: Knight with weapon meeting destiny

parts.note: a lance is a weapon
one's lot is one's fate or destiny

explanation.surface: A mounted warrior with a spear meets his fate.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancelot was the most famous knight of King Arthur's Round Table.

clue.text: Arrest outlaw turning up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it

explanation.surface: Police seize a bandit who has just appeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' looks like arriving, but it reverses BAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To nab is informal for to catch or arrest.

clue.text: Shop gets you tired ultimately, having several floors?

parts.note: a store is a shop
ye is an old form of you

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word tired

explanation.surface: Shopping wears you out in the end, with so many levels to climb.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: a building with storeys.
explanation.definitionFit: Storeyed describes a building divided into levels, so having several floors.

clue.text: Composer another wrote an opera about?

definitions.meaning: Rossini wrote The ... of Seville, an opera about a hairdresser

explanation.surface: A music writer about whom a fellow musician wrote an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Barber is both the surname of an American composer and the trade of Rossini's opera hero, Figaro.
